avalancheActivity.comment:
Above 1800 m: On sufficiently steep slopes, the layer of light snow may slide over the older snowpack, potentially triggering small to medium-sized avalanches—either spontaneously or, more likely, due to additional loading (risk level 2).
Below 1800 m: On steep slopes, conditions exist for the triggering of generally small-sized avalanches (risk level 1).
avalancheActivity.highlights: Snow accompanied by drifting, with the accumulation of a new layer of snow—more substantial in southwestern mountain massifs.

snowpackStructure.comment:
Above 1800 m: A new layer of powder snow will settle on top of the existing snowpack—which is largely frozen near the ground—along with a recently accumulated layer (10–15 cm) of snow. This will result in a 20–40 cm layer characterized by low cohesion between the crystals themselves and in relation to the underlying snowpack. Strong winds will facilitate the formation of large accumulations (exceeding 60–80 cm) on sheltered slopes, as well as wind slabs at higher altitudes.
Below 1800 m: A new snow layer of 15–25 cm will accumulate in some areas.

weatherForecast.comment:
The weather will turn significantly colder. The sky will be mostly cloudy, and snowfall will occur over extensive areas. Precipitation amounts of 10–20 l/m² are expected across all mountain massifs; in the northern Eastern Carpathians and the Southern Carpathians, these amounts will locally reach 20–40 l/m², while in the western part of the Southern Carpathians, they may exceed 40 l/m² in isolated areas. Snow accumulation will reach 15–25 cm in most mountain massifs, with over 25–35 cm expected in the northern Eastern Carpathians and the Southern Carpathians. The wind will blow moderately, with intensifications—on November 23, primarily in the Southern and Curvature Carpathians, and subsequently on November 24, mainly in the Eastern Carpathians—reaching speeds of 70–90 km/h (and 90–120 km/h along the ridges), causing drifting snow or blowing snow.

Minimum temperatures above 1800 m: dropping from -8…-3°C to -17…-11°C; maximum temperatures above 1800 m: dropping from -5…-1°C to -16…-9°C. The altitude of the 0°C isotherm: descending from 1000–1700 m to 300–800 m by the end of the period, with the lowest values ​​occurring in the northern massifs.

weatherReview.comment:
The weather has turned colder compared to previous days. Widespread mixed precipitation occurred at lower altitudes, while at higher elevations—above 1,800 meters—it fell as snow, resulting in a new snow accumulation of 10–15 cm. The wind intensified, particularly along mountain ridges, causing the snow to drift or be blown about.
On November 22, at 14:00, snow depths recorded at meteorological station sites were as follows:
40 cm at Omu Peak, 16 cm at Lăcăuți, 14 cm at Iezer Peak, 12 cm at Țarcu, 11 cm at Bâlea-Lac, 10 cm at Călimani, and 2 cm at Penteleu.

avalancheActivity.comment:
Above 1800 m: On sufficiently steep slopes, the layer of light snow may slide over the older snowpack, potentially triggering small to medium-sized avalanches—either spontaneously or, more likely, due to additional loading on the snowpack (risk level 2).
Below 1800m:  On steep slopes, it may slide over the ground or over an existing thin layer, triggering avalanches that are generally small in size (risk 1).
